title: Monotonicity of polynomial threshold classes
statement: Let $k,k',n\in\mathbb N$ with $k\le k'$. Every $\{-1,1\}$-valued function on $\{0,1\}^n$ that has a polynomial threshold representation of degree at most $k$ also has one of degree at most $k'$.
hypotheses_covered: k and k′ are natural numbers
replaced: For every $n,k,k'\in\mathbb N$ with $k\leq k'$, every $\{-1,1\}$-valued function on $\{0,1\}^{n}$ represented by $\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(p((-1)^{x_1},\ldots,(-1)^{x_n}))$ for a real multilinear polynomial $p$ of degree at most $k$ also admits such a representation of degree at most $k'$, where $\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(t)=1$ for $t\geq0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$.
